Title: Does Dabbler trigger on an ended action?

Messages.Author: Gr33n
Messages.Body:
During an action, a vampire with dabbler uses 3 disciplines.

Change of target is played.

Can dabbler trigger?

Messages.Author: mipopo3
Messages.Body:
Dabbler

Warning: Spoiler!

Archetype. Trifle.
Put this card on a vampire you control. Once each turn, after an action (successful or not) is resolved during which this vampire used 3 or more Disciplines to play cards, this vampire can either burn 1 blood to unlock or gain 1 blood. A vampire can have only one archetype.

Change of Target

Warning: Spoiler!

Only usable if this minion is blocked, before block resolution.
Unlock this minion. The action ends (unsuccessfully). This minion cannot perform the same action again this turn.

Action ended, not canceled, so "Yes", you get the blood.

Messages.Author: mipopo3
Messages.Body:
So after Tangle Atropos' Hand

Warning: Spoiler!

Only usable if a minion attempts to block.
Potence Cancel the action and unlock this vampire. (The action is not blocked. Do not lock the blocking minion.)
Temporis As Potence above, and if an action card was played, take it back in your hand (discard down afterward).
Superior Temporis As Temporis above, and this vampire gets +1 stealth during their next action this turn.

You do not get the blood. ( or DI)

Messages.Author: Gr33n
Messages.Body:
Dabbler not being an action modifier isn't a good enough argument in itself.

"after an action is resolved" and "after action resolution" seem to be the same window.

Actions that have ended before or during resolution do not allow playing "after action resolution" cards.

For which reason would Dabbler being an optional effect allow it to be used when the action is no longer active?

Daring the dawn has a ruling that the damage is still applied. Difference is that daring the dawn is a mandatory effect.

Similar to how Outside the hourglass damage must resolve even if during the prevention window it opens, alpha glint ends the combat.

Or an action ending due to sup Mirror walk still has the vampire burned from Millicent vampire hunter.

Would be nice to know the official answer either way.

Name: Dabbler

Archetype. Trifle.
Put this card on a vampire you control. Once each turn, after an action (successful or not) is resolved during which this vampire used 3 or more Disciplines to play cards, this vampire can either burn 1 blood to unlock or gain 1 blood. A vampire can have only one archetype.

The answer is: No. Once the action ends, you cannot use effects that are usable during a action. "after an action (successful or not) is resolved" happens after resolution of the action.

This effect is not a delayed triggered effect that has to be resolved due to a previous condition met.

>
> "after an action is resolved" and "after action resolution" seem to be the same window.
>
Correct.

Messages.Author: Bloodartist
Messages.Body:
I feel we have made mountains out of molehills in this topic. I also wonder whether Ankha either misread Dabbler or forgot how he has defined things in the past.

1.
"Action ends" = "Action resolves unsuccessfully".
If you play change of target on an action, the action cannot be attempted again. -> Action resolved. You can use dabbler just fine because the action reached resolution. The time window (whatever it is) is not in any way different from other ways of resolving an action, whether its successful resolution or action being blocked.

2. Yes, dabbler is not a delayed trigger. Dabbler is a "once per turn" effect that can be performed after an action has resolved (with conditions).

3. The wording of the timing window is technically the same as with freak drive, which is a card that can be played after action resolution. The difference is that freak drive is an action modifier, and thus must be played during an action. Same is not true for dabbler which is a master card. So this begs the question, can dabblers effect be used later in the turn (which is also "after action resolution") as long as its condition is met? If we read the cardtext as english language and not as defined rules phrases, I would say yes.

ps. (not related to ruling in question) I would also like to point out for the umpteenth time that much of the confusion stems from using open-ended words such as "after" and "before" when defining timing windows. This is illogical and unintuitive and confuses players. It would be far simpler to use wording such as "effect happens/card is playable at the end of the action", in which case it would be clear that the effect must happen within the action, not next year which is also 'after' the action. If things would happen at the same time, then appropriate player could decide the order. Everything would be tidy.

Smoking craters tell no tales.
—Tex talks Battletech

No, it's "Once each turn, after an action (successful or not) is resolved during which this vampire used 3 or more Disciplines to play cards", you cannot use it in your discard or transfer phase, you have to use it right after an action (successful or not) is resolved. Messages.Body:

> No, it's "Once each turn, after an action (successful or not) is resolved during which this vampire used 3 or more Disciplines to play cards", you cannot use it in your discard or transfer phase, you have to use it right after an action (successful or not) is resolved. The "once each turn" indicates you can use this effect only once per turn, not that you can use it at any point of the turn.
>
Core Rulebook:
Action modifier cards: The acting minion can play these cards to modify their action at any time before action resolution.
Dabbler:
"Once each turn, after an action (successful or not) is resolved"
There is no time restriction after action resolution; the only restriction is the end of the turn.
There is no "in minion phase", "before untap"; there is no "after performing" restriction.
The only condition to be met is:
1) 3 Disciplines were used (action can be successful or not, but not canceled).
2) The turn didn't end.

Messages.Author: mipopo3
Messages.Body:
Action can resolve in only two ways:
1) Successful
2) Unsuccessful
Thus, a resolution occurred.
Action ends with a mirror walk, or a change of target does not skip the declaration of the resolution.
Resolution must be declared.

Wording that should match the rulebook should be:
"Action ends: Skip block and action resolution"
With this, you make it clear.
